Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months since the prior anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at the same level
Symptoms include significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)
Post-operative physical exam findings are concordant with the individual's symptoms

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with BOTH of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks; provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks
Post-operative imaging (performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion) shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post-operative MRI/CT findings are concordant with the individual's symptoms
Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)

Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following: individual is a never-smoker; individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis (TOC: S11.1.2)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months since the prior anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at the same level

Symptoms include BOTH of the following: significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.); unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam findings include ANY of the following: dermatomal sensory deficit; motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness); reflex changes; shoulder abduction relief sign; nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver); unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks; provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks; epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery
Post-operative imaging (performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion) shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)

Post-operative MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation); synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst; central/lateral/foraminal stenosis; osteophytes
Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)

Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following: individual is a never-smoker; individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Radiculopathy with Pseudoarthrosis (TOC: S11.1.3)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months since the prior anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at the same level

Symptoms include ANY of the following: upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness of hands); gait disturbance; new-onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; frequent falls

Physical exam findings include ANY of the following: grip and release test; ataxic gait; hyperreflexia; Hoffmann sign; Babinski sign; tandem walking test demonstrating ataxia; inverted brachial radial reflex; increased muscle tone or spasticity; clonus; myelopathic hand
Post-operative imaging (performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion) shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)

Post-operative MRI/CT shows findings that are concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that are caused by EITHER of the following: cervical spinal cord compression; cervical spinal stenosis
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level > Myelopathy with Pseudoarthrosis (TOC: S11.1.4)

Non-Indications: Isolated axial neck pain without radiculopathy or myelopathy is not a covered indication unless accompanied by pseudoarthrosis and meeting all criteria for 'Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis' (including >6 months post-op, functional impairment, failed conservative care, and concordant imaging).
Surgery performed less than six (6) months after the prior anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at the same level.
Absence of pseudoarthrosis on post-operative imaging performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion.

Failure to demonstrate less than clinically meaningful improvement with required conservative management (analgesics/NSAIDs and exercise for 6 weeks for neck pain; analgesics/NSAIDs, exercise, or injections for 6 weeks for radiculopathy).
Presence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).
Failure to document nicotine-free status (never-smoker or 6 weeks abstinence validated by objective cotinine testing) for neck pain and radiculopathy indications.
Important criteria & exceptions: Repeat ACDF at the same level is considered medically necessary only when performed for ANY of the listed conditions (Malposition/Failure, Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis, Radiculopathy with Pseudoarthrosis, Myelopathy with Pseudoarthrosis) when ALL associated criteria are met.
For 'Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis', conservative care must include BOTH prescription strength analgesics/NSAIDs and a provider-directed exercise program for six (6) weeks.

For 'Radiculopathy with Pseudoarthrosis', conservative care must include at least TWO of the following: prescription strength analgesics/NSAIDs, provider-directed exercise program, or epidural steroid injection(s)/selective nerve root block(s) for six (6) weeks.

Nicotine-free status must be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed, unless the individual is a never-smoker.
Post-operative imaging must be performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion to demonstrate pseudoarthrosis.
Documentation required: Post-operative imaging reports (MRI/CT) performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior cervical fusion showing pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s).
Post-operative MRI/CT reports showing findings concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings (e.g., neural structure compression, cervical spinal cord compression, or cervical spinal stenosis).
Documentation of conservative management including prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for six (6) weeks.
Documentation of provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks.
Documentation of epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery (for Radiculopathy indication).

Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed, or documentation of never-smoker status.
Documentation of absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders.
